title: Enhancing Healthcare System Resilience: A Complex Adaptive Systems Approach to Clinical Decision Support and Cybersecurity Governance Using BPMN and DMN
content: Healthcare ecosystems operate as Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) where heterogeneous human and technical agents,including clinicians, patients, Electronic Health Records (EHRs), medical devices, cloud providers, and regulatory auditors, interact non-linearly across multiple scales. While digitalization enhances care coordination, embedding complex clinical and cybersecurity decision rules directly within operational process models creates rigid, opaque "black-box" architectures that struggle to adapt to evolving clinical protocols and zero-day cyber threats. Grounded in CAS theory and model-driven systems engineering, this study proposes an integrated socio-technical framework that combines the Object Management Group’s (OMG) Decision Model and Notation (DMN) and Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) to simultaneously govern Clinical Decision Support (CDS) and cybersecurity compliance. First, we formulate a mathematical state-space representation of the healthcare CAS, demonstrating how DMN Decision Services act as bounded homeostatic controllers. Second, we analyze baseline domain implementations across infrastructure compliance, clinical LACE readmission risk scoring via HL7 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) and CDS Hooks, and cloud-based Camunda "Burdens of Proof" (BoP) security governance. Finally, we synthesize these layers into a novel Unified Healthcare CDS and Cybersecurity Authorization DMN Model. Our findings demonstrate that separating decision logic from process orchestration enhances adaptive capacity, compresses requirements validation feedback loops, and provides explainable sub-decision audit trails for both point-of-care clinicians and GDPR security auditors.
